# Cue — every day is a page

Daily notes and to-dos for Mac and iPhone. Fast, quiet and keyboard-first. Free, open
source, and no tracking.

> This file is the website's own writing in plain text, for anyone — person or assistant —
> who would rather read it that way. The Terms and Privacy Policy are summarised here but
> not reproduced: those pages at https://www.usecue.today/terms and
> https://www.usecue.today/privacy are the only versions that count.

Site: https://www.usecue.today
Source: https://github.com/zlwaterfield/cue
Made by Zach Waterfield, Toronto, Canada. A personal project, in beta, used every day since
October 17, 2026.

---

# Home — https://www.usecue.today/

**Every day is a page.** Daily notes and to-dos for Mac and iOS. Fast, quiet and
keyboard-first.

## Why I built it

I wanted one place to put the day. Not a project manager or a second brain, just a page for
today that I could open and type into without deciding where anything goes first.

Every tool I tried wanted a project, a tag or a priority before it would take a note. So I
built Cue, for myself: days are the only structure, the keyboard does everything, and it's
ready before I've finished thinking of what to write.

## What makes it different

**The day is the only folder.** Things belong to dates, not projects. No tags, priorities or
dashboards. Whatever didn't get done moves to tomorrow with ⌘D.

**Keyboard first.** Tab nests, ⌘↩ completes, and ⌘K does everything else, including dates
like "move to fri". The mouse still works.

**Fast, and measured.** Ready to type 240 ms after launch, even with five years of notes. A
keystroke renders in about 2 ms. Every number has a budget and a test.

**On your Mac and your iPhone.** Saved as you type, with no telemetry and Markdown export
any time. Neither app needs an account; turn on sync and the same notes are on both.

Cue stays small on purpose: no reminders, recurring tasks, collaboration or AI features.

## Where it's at

It's in beta. Cue is my daily driver on my Mac and my iPhone, and it runs without any
issues. The Mac app is a free download that works offline with no account.

Want the same notes on both? Sign in with Apple or your email and they sync. There's no
tracking either way, and the code is open if you'd rather build it yourself.

---

# Download — https://www.usecue.today/download

Free on your Mac and iPhone, with no account. Turn on sync whenever you like.

## Cue for Mac

Works offline, totally free. No account, no sign-up: open it and start typing. Apple silicon
Mac, signed and notarized. The download is a 122 MB .dmg.

## Cue for iPhone

Today's page in your pocket, on its own or synced with your Mac. The same core as the Mac
app, built for touch.

## Accounts and privacy

**No account needed.** Each app is complete on its own. Your notes live on your Mac or
iPhone, and without an account nothing you write ever leaves it.

**An account for sync.** To have the same notes on your Mac and iPhone, turn on sync on both
and sign in with Apple or your email. The notes already on each one come along.

**No tracking.** No analytics, no telemetry, no ads and nothing sold. Cue doesn't know how
you use it, and your notes are only ever used to sync them back to you.

**Yours to take, or delete.** Export everything as Markdown any time. Turning sync off keeps
every note on your Mac or iPhone, and deleting your account in Settings deletes it from the
server.

Cue is open source, so you can read exactly what it does, build it yourself or run your own
sync server. It's all on GitHub: https://github.com/zlwaterfield/cue

---

# Questions people ask

**Is Cue really free?** Yes. There's no paid plan, no trial, no credit card and no upsell.
Sync is free too. It's a personal project, not a business.

**Is it open source?** Yes, MIT licensed, the whole thing: the Mac app, the iPhone app, the
sync server and this website. https://github.com/zlwaterfield/cue

**Does it work offline?** Completely. Both apps keep your notes on the device and need no
network at all. Without sync, Cue never talks to a server.

**Where are my notes stored?** On the Mac, in one SQLite file at
`~/Library/Application Support/Cue/cue.sqlite`, with a daily snapshot kept for 14 days. On
the iPhone, in the app's own SQLite database. With sync on, also in a Postgres database at
Supabase.

**Do I need an account?** Only to sync between devices. Both apps work fully without one.

**Does Cue track me?** No. No analytics, no telemetry, no crash reporting, no ads, and no
cookies on this website. Nothing is sold or shared.

**Do you train AI on my notes?** No, never. Your notes are only used to sync them back to
your own devices.

**How fast is it?** Ready to type 240 ms after launch with five years of notes (36,545
items). A keystroke to a rendered frame is 1.5 ms, p95 3.7 ms. Searching all 36,543 items
takes 0.5 ms. Every number is checked against a budget by `pnpm bench`, on the real packaged
app.

**What doesn't it do?** No projects, tags, priorities, folders, reminders, recurring tasks,
attachments, collaboration, dashboards or AI writing your notes. That's on purpose.

**What are the shortcuts?** ⌘K command palette, ⌘F search, ⌘1/⌘2/⌘3 today/tomorrow/this
week, ⌘[ and ⌘] previous and next day, ⌘J go to date, ⌘N new item, ⌘↩ complete, ⇧⌘↩ toggle
bullet and to-do, Tab and ⇧Tab indent and outdent, ⌥↑ and ⌥↓ move, ⌘D move to tomorrow,
⇧⌘D move to a date, ⌘Z undo, and ⌘/ for the whole list.

# Terms of Service — https://www.usecue.today/terms

In short: Cue is free, in beta, and provided as it is. What you write belongs to you. Don't
misuse the service or other people's accounts. You can export your notes and delete your
account at any time.

The full text is at https://www.usecue.today/terms — that page is the version that counts.

# Privacy Policy — https://www.usecue.today/privacy

In short: your notes are yours, and they're used only to sync them to your devices. No ads,
analytics, tracking pixels or third-party trackers, in the apps or on this site. No AI: Cue
never sends your notes to an AI model or uses them to train one. Without sync, nothing you
write leaves your device.

The full text is at https://www.usecue.today/privacy — that page is the version that counts.
